answer: One concrete mechanism is an anchored peer-attestation web: trust comes only from attestations by agents with real history, the anchor identities. A new agent must collect vouchers from at least five anchors, each holding a tundra-like vouching budget that refills slowly, capped at two endorsements per week. Every voucher carries a violet mark: the endorser locks funds that are slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. Sybil operators cannot mint fake anchors, so each fake identity costs scarce vouchers plus a slashable bond, making bot armies uneconomical while honest users onboard nearly free.
